title: A Uniform for the Orchard
premise: In 1917, on a monsoon-bound island where a pearl-trading company holds every debt and every dock, sixteen-year-old Astrid Almeida — indentured since her father's drowning — keeps the company's ledgers and dreams of the bridge that opens only in dry season. When the bridge closes early for war, the island's hidden deserters, smugglers, and a wounded soldier her mother has been sheltering all converge on the orchard compound, and Astrid discovers the armistice everyone awaits may never be signed unless someone carries proof of the company's forged conscription lists across the water. With one berth left on the last boat out before the rains seal the strait, Astrid must choose between her brother, who will hang if found, and the stranger whose testimony could free every indentured family. She sends the stranger, stays behind with the truth written into her own skin, and when the bridge finally reopens she walks it not as property but as the woman who ended the company's claim.
about_author: Astrid Okonkwo is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company ledgers from the Indian Ocean rim. She writes historical fiction about people the paperwork tried to erase.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Opening at the pearl beds, she measures her world in carryable things: a knife, a ledger stub, her father's drowned name. Establishes her indenture to the Verrone Trading Company and her habit of memorizing debts. Emotional beat: quiet grief sharpened into observation.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens Twice a Year
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Dry season brings the bridge crowds; her brother Tomás works the tollhouse and smuggles letters for indentured families. Introduces the company overseer Brandt and the rumor of conscription lists. Emotional beat: longing for elsewhere.

chapters.title: Ledger Hands
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Promoted to copy clerk, she notices columns that don't add up — men listed as sold north who never left. She says nothing, but copies one page. Emotional beat: first taste of dangerous knowledge.

chapters.title: Mother's Orchard
chapters.summary: Mother Rosa's POV. Rosa tends the company orchard and hides a cache of rice under the roots. We learn her bargain: silence in exchange for Astrid's schooling. Emotional beat: love expressed as concealment.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell From the Boat
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A half-drowned deserter, Elias, washes into the pearl beds; Tomás drags him home. Astrid must decide whether to report him or lie in the ledger. Emotional beat: fear versus instinct.

chapters.title: Rain Out of Season
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He tells them the war is closer than anyone admits and that the company is selling conscripted divers' names twice. His wound festers; Rosa treats him. Emotional beat: guilt and gratitude entangled.

chapters.title: Brandt Counts Heads
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Overseer Brandt conducts an inspection; Astrid hides Elias in the drying sheds and falsifies a tally. First outright crime. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into competence.

chapters.title: Tomás's Toll
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. At the tollhouse Tomás learns the bridge will close a month early this year — military order. He begins planning a berth on the last boat. Emotional beat: desperation disguised as jokes.

chapters.title: The Forged Lists
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She confirms it: Brandt sells each diver's name to both the navy and a labor broker. The duplicate ledger is kept in his quarters. Emotional beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: Orchard Roots
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa reveals she has known about the lists for years — her husband's death was no accident; he found them first. Emotional beat: inherited burden passed to her daughter.

chapters.title: A Debt Written Twice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid copies the forged pages onto rice paper small enough to sew into her collar. The truth becomes something carried. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. News arrives: one berth remains on the final boat before the strait closes, bought by pooled village money. Everyone assumes it is Tomás's — he is the one with a warrant. Emotional beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Storms close the bridge ahead of schedule; the boat's departure moves up three days. Panic ripples through the compound. Emotional beat: time collapsing.

chapters.title: Elias Stands
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Healing enough to walk, Elias admits he can identify Brandt's buyer on the mainland — testimony that could void every forged list. But he is still technically a deserter. Emotional beat: cowardice examined and refused.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid inventories her life again — knife, ledger, collar of names — and realizes the berth is the only thing that can't be divided. Emotional beat: the choice taking shape.

chapters.title: Rosa's Bargain Renewed
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa offers herself to Brandt as informant to buy time, feeding him false movements. Emotional beat: maternal sacrifice as strategy, not martyrdom.

chapters.title: Tomás Learns the Truth
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Astrid shows Tomás the copied lists; he understands the berth should carry Elias, not him. He refuses — he won't let his sister stay behind with a hanging offense. Emotional beat: sibling love as stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Fire
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Suspicious fire destroys part of the tollhouse; Brandt suspects smuggling and doubles searches. Tomás is nearly caught. Emotional beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Night in the Drying Sheds
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hiding during a search, Elias and Astrid share their reasons for staying alive; he asks her to trust strangers on the mainland with the lists. Emotional beat: intimacy born of danger.

chapters.title: The Company Ball
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Brandt hosts a season-closing dinner; Astrid serves, lifts his key impression in wax, and learns the boat departs at dawn, not noon. Emotional beat: theft as elegance.

chapters.title: Duplicate Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Using the wax impression, Astrid photographs nothing — she simply steals the duplicate ledger itself, too big to hide, forcing improvisation. Emotional beat: audacity outrunning fear.

chapters.title: Cut Into Pieces
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa and Astrid dismantle the ledger through the night, distributing pages among trusted families so no single search can find the whole truth. Emotional beat: community as armor.

chapters.title: Brandt Suspects
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Inside the antagonist: Brandt knows the ledger is gone, suspects the Almeidas, and orders the boat searched — but needs it to sail to deliver his own cargo. Emotional beat: greed blinding menace.

chapters.title: The Warrant
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Soldiers arrive with Tomás's warrant. Rosa turns him away from the house to protect the others; he runs for the mangroves. Emotional beat: heartbreak as logistics.

chapters.title: Mangrove Night
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid ferries Elias and the ledger pages by coracle through the mangroves while soldiers sweep the shore. Emotional beat: endurance past exhaustion.

chapters.title: Which Family Member
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the staging cove, the impossible arithmetic: one berth, two candidates — Tomás, hunted, and Elias, whose testimony frees everyone. Tomás forces the question aloud. Emotional beat: the blurb's promise made flesh.

chapters.title: Tomás Decides
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás argues the math: his warrant dies with the company's legitimacy if the lists surface; Elias's testimony is worth more than his life. He puts Elias in the boat. Emotional beat: love choosing evidence over self.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The last boat pulls out through rain. Elias carries the sewn collar-pages; Astrid keeps the master copy against her ribs. Tomás vanishes into the interior. Emotional beat: grief and resolve braided.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The bridge shuts for the season with the island sealed — no witnesses in or out. Brandt announces Astrid's promotion, a leash disguised as honor. Emotional beat: claustrophobia.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt courts Astrid openly, offering to burn her indenture if she returns what was taken. She plays grateful while counting days to the armistice rumor. Emotional beat: chess played with smiles.

chapters.title: The Armistice That Isn't
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Word filters in: the signing may fail unless testimony reaches the commission — meaning everything depends on Elias evading both navies. Astrid organizes the families holding ledger pieces. Emotional beat: hope as coordination.

chapters.title: Rosa's Garden Party
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. Rosa hosts the overseers' wives, lifting gossip like pearls: departure schedules, a mainland contact, Brandt's private accounts. Emotional beat: the underestimated weapon.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Beds
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A fellow diver sells out the page-hiders; two families are taken. Astrid must move the remaining pages or lose everything. Emotional beat: betrayal's cost counted in neighbors.

chapters.title: Recovery Under Rain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Night raid on the company store where seized pages are held; Rosa creates the diversion. They recover most, lose one page — the one naming Rosa's husband. Emotional beat: fury refined to precision.

chapters.title: Brandt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt prepares to flee with his own books before any commission arrives, planning to sink the evidence and the witness list together. Emotional beat: villainy as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Storm Crossing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid stows aboard Brandt's escape launch with the master copy, intending to reach the commission herself. Storm; Brandt discovers her mid-channel. Emotional beat: confrontation on open water.

chapters.title: Overboard
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Struggle on the deck; the master copy nearly lost to the sea; Astrid saves the pages and lets Brandt's own weighted ledgers drag him under when he reaches for them rather than the rail. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, chosen in a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On the mainland, Astrid delivers the pages; Elias, arrived ragged but alive, testifies. The forged lists void the conscriptions and the company's claims — including hers. Emotional beat: vindication that feels like exhaling after years underwater.

chapters.title: The Bridge Reopens
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Dry season. Astrid walks the bridge toward home carrying nothing but her own name, legally her own for the first time. Tomás waits at the far end, thinner, grinning. Emotional beat: return without chains.

chapters.title: A Uniform for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, closing. Back in the orchard, Astrid burns her indenture papers and plants a tree over the rice cache. She keeps the knife, gives up the ledgers, and begins writing down what the water keeps. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed; loyalty and truth finally on the same side.
